Instead trim positions slowly and utilise the new capital to chase other markets.

Fuck what your personal charts look like on social trading platforms.

Hold on to positions that you don't want to chase in the future.

Trim profit instead of full closing.

Chinese AI labs are forcing the market to compete on the cost of useful intelligence.

Export controls restricted Chinese labs’ access to advanced NVIDIA chips. Staying competitive meant extracting more performance from the hardware available.

In training, Deepseek kept GPUs working while data moved between them and shifted to lower-precision formats that halve memory and compute.

The bigger savings came in serving: sparse models activate only a fraction of their parameters per token, and redesigned attention cut the memory cost of long contexts. The result is models that are cheaper to build and far cheaper to run.

Chinese open-weight models went from under 1.2% of weekly token consumption on OpenRouter in late 2024 to a majority in 2026. 

OpenRouter is a small percentage of global token volumes and its users are price-elastic so this should not be read as global market share. It does show that users will choose cheaper models when switching is easy and performance is good enough.

Cheaper inference also has strategic value for China. These models can already run on domestic accelerators and reduce the country’s dependence on foreign hardware for inference. China still relies largely on foreign chips for frontier training.

China will not have full compute independence until its labs can train frontier models at scale on domestic infrastructure.

MYRIAD IS DRILLING INTO A HISTORICAL 655 MILLION POUND URANIUM ENDOWMENT

That is the scale of the opportunity at Copper Mountain, and Myriad Uranium is now generating the modern data needed to determine how much of it can ultimately be converted into a compliant resource.

These figures are historical and conceptual, not current mineral resources, but they were based on extensive technical work and access to Union Pacific’s enormous dataset. Around 2,000 boreholes were drilled historically at Copper Mountain, with Union Pacific investing an estimated C$125 million in today’s money.

Phase II drilling is now advancing quickly:

🔹 Lucky Cliff: initial results released and assays pending
🔹 Gem: drilling completed and results ahead
🔹 Hesitation: drill team now on site

Over the past decade, 200+ companies have been removed from the S&P 500 Index and a similar number added. A 2023 study found ~180 stocks have been replaced since 2015 - about one-third of the index. Of the 2010 roster, ~185 tickers were gone by 2026. 

The index is a "living" basket. It promotes what is working and demotes what has broken. That is active management with a committee and a rulebook.

The same lesson applies to individual “great stocks.”

$LULU printed $511 at the end of 2023; it is now around $122 (~80% decline). 

$TTD ran to ~$140 in December 2024, then suffered an ~90% drawdown.

$NKE and $BA remained household names and index members while years of gains vanished.

That is the point most buy-and-hold sermons skip. Quality is not a substitute for timing. Leadership decays. Growth slows. Multiples compress. A stock can be an excellent business and still destroy capital if you own it through a Stage 4 decline. 

The index itself does not “hold forever.” It sells the laggards - often late, but it sells them.

The aim is not to marry a ticker. It is to own leadership while it is leadership - so we can hold onto the years of gains that disappear in months. Another reason why semis are hard (and more broadly, equities), and no longer the hot ball of money is because things are no longer linear, easy to understand

Longing most "global trends" generate the most returns - in 2021, you long crypto (it was the biggest thing); 2023, financials, 2025, semis

These homerun trades often focus on one core theme: Demand is increasing, this benefits. And most homerun trades, if you look in the past 5 years, have all come from this simple seed

The moment a thematic starts becoming more complex, it fails. Investors become uncertain if what they're holding is what will be needed. And that's where AI is right now.

Take a look at AVGO's earnings. AVGO reported extraordinary numbers - F3Q revenue +85.5% YoY - and introduced FY27/FY28 AI revenue targets of $115B/$230B. FY28 potentially supports >$30 EPS. 

But AVGO sold off because FY27 was below buyside expectations of ~$130–150B and the growth increasingly depends on OpenAI + Anthropic. Around 15GW of the roughly 20GW FY28 deployment discussed comes from those two customers. 

On the other hand, software, which was thought to be left for dead, is incredibly strong. SNOW is up 16% - Product growth accelerated sharply, about half the acceleration came from AI products, CoCo adoption reached ~63%, cRPO accelerated, and margins are holding up better than expected. 

All of a sudden, software may be the enterprise control plane for AI agents? No one knows. And so the AI trade is basically unwinding on itself, because its so hard to forecast the future

Markets are ever-evolving, and so, IMO, it's more worthwhile to figure out where the puck will be 6 months from now

These homerun trades often focus on one core theme: Demand is increasing, this benefits. And most homerun trades, if you look in the past 5 years, have all come from this simple seed

The moment a thematic starts becoming more complex, it fails. Investors become uncertain if what they're holding is what will be needed. And that's where AI is right now.

Take a look at AVGO's earnings. AVGO reported extraordinary numbers - F3Q revenue +85.5% YoY - and introduced FY27/FY28 AI revenue targets of $115B/$230B. FY28 potentially supports >$30 EPS. 

But AVGO sold off because FY27 was below buyside expectations of ~$130–150B and the growth increasingly depends on OpenAI + Anthropic. Around 15GW of the roughly 20GW FY28 deployment discussed comes from those two customers. 

On the other hand, software, which was thought to be left for dead, is incredibly strong. SNOW is up 16% - Product growth accelerated sharply, about half the acceleration came from AI products, CoCo adoption reached ~63%, cRPO accelerated, and margins are holding up better than expected. 

All of a sudden, software may be the enterprise control plane for AI agents? No one knows. And so the AI trade is basically unwinding on itself, because its so hard to forecast the future

Markets are ever-evolving, and so, IMO, it's more worthwhile to figure out where the puck will be 6 months from now
